narrative:
The model predicts you have a 51% chance of failing your final year, which is just over the threshold that requires you to take remedial courses. This means the school will obligate you to attend extra classes to help strengthen your performance before moving forward.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. By far the strongest factor is that you have already failed one class in the past. Among students who passed, the average number of past failures is zero, so this history strongly pushes the model toward expecting you to fail again. Your very low amount of free time after school is the second most important factor; surprisingly, this actually pulls the prediction slightly toward passing, because students with very low free time tend to do better than those with more unstructured time. Third, the good quality of your family relationships also nudges the outcome slightly in a positive direction, as strong family support is generally linked to better results.

Even though these last two elements help a little, they are not enough to overcome the weight of your past academic setback. To improve, you should focus on preventing any further failures by creating a realistic study schedule, seeking extra help early in difficult subjects, and using your strong family support to stay accountable. Addressing absences, which are already higher than average, will also be important. Taking the remedial courses seriously gives you a clear opportunity to close these gaps. (248 words)
